processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Monocrystals with up to 10 cm length were grown by the Bridgman method (10–15 mm/h pulling rate). The crystal growth with subsequent cooling occurred within a time period of about 12 h.

processing_steps.method: etching with ammonium persulfate ((NH4)2S2O8) followed by orientation using a special laser light-figure method
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The monocrystals were etched by ammonium persulfate and oriented using a special laser light-figure method. This is the terminal as-grown state; the sample was used without any further heat treatment.

structures.overall_structure: Single crystal (monocrystal), as-grown; Fe-Al solid-solution matrix with rare globular AlN inclusions. No second-phase carbides present because no heat treatment was applied.

inclusions: rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm, identified by EDX analysis

characterization_methods.technique: energy-dispersive X-ray analysis (EDX) in scanning electron microscopy (SEM)
characterization_methods.purpose: qualitative precipitate/inclusion analysis and identification of globular inclusions in the monocrystals
characterization_methods.key_findings: The monocrystals contained rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm.

characterization_methods.technique: optical microscopy of etched specimens (metallographic inspection)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: optical microscope; etching with alcoholic 10% nitric acid solution
characterization_methods.key_findings: Without heat treatment no carbides were found in all monocrystals.
Compositions of all alloys are listed in Table 1; the Fe-17%Al monocrystal had a real Al content of 16.8 at.% (8.9 wt.-%) with C 70, Si 140 wt.ppm, Cu 50, Mo 90.

unmapped_findings: The heat-treated variant of the Fe-17%Al monocrystal (with 70 ppm C) — 14 days at 320 °C with concurrent 100 MPa loading in <111> direction — contained thin carbides; without loading much less carbides were observed. This finding concerns a heat-treated condition and does NOT apply to the as-grown sample extracted here.
No carbides were found in the as-grown monocrystals (Fe-16%Al and Fe-17%Al) when no heat treatment was applied, consistent with the as-grown state of this sample.

The Fe-17%Al monocrystal (Table 1, row 17, Monocrystals) has a real Al content of 16.8 at.% (8.9 wt.-%) with impurities C 70 wt.ppm, Si 140 wt.ppm, and other elements Cu 50, Mo 90 (the nominal composition is 17 at.% Al).

Noticeable short-range ordering (K-state) develops in binary Fe-Al alloys with Al contents in the range 13–18 at.% at temperatures below 600 °C after solidification (highest degree at 250 °C); this applies to the Fe-17%Al alloy class but was not measured specifically for the as-grown monocrystal of this sample.
